Was previously modeled at 180 seats (inherited from kerosene_short) with no real program at that scale. Moved from long-haul to short-haul: hydrogen's poor volumetric energy density makes long-haul the hardest real case, not the easiest (confirmed by the supplied research - no hydrogen option appears for wide-body/very-large aircraft at all). Real anchor: Airbus ZEROe turbofan concept, 120-200 seats, 2,000+ nm range, real 2035 target service entry. Caveat: Airbus itself narrowed focus to the fuel-cell-powered ZEROe variant specifically in 2025, a real signal of even greater timeline uncertainty than the 2035 combustion-concept date alone suggests. CAPEX multiplier set to 1.31x conventional CAPEX: a detailed EU industry study sizes a hydrogen fuel-cell/turbine hybrid 165-passenger short-range aircraft at exactly this ratio - an exact seat-count match for this row (replaces an earlier 1.6x placeholder, then a 1.13x general Hoelzen-2021 acquisition-cost figure). HC and CO set to exactly 0: hydrogen combustion contains no carbon, so hydrocarbon and carbon-monoxide emissions are physically zero, not an estimate. NOx and smoke number are unchanged - no real hydrogen-turbofan EDB entry exists to source them from; remain a documented gap. lifetime_years set to the evidence-based recommended value: 25 years (A15-A16 hydrogen combustion rule: use host airframe lifetime (narrow-body-class aircraft, 25yr) - hydrogen propulsion itself has no observed commercial fleet lifetime). Was 24 years.
